title: Solid Shapes, Nets and Surface Area
seo_title: Solids and Nets – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify properties of plane shapes and solids; name solids from their nets; find the surface area of cubes and cuboids. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on solid shapes: cubes, cuboids, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres, nets and the surface area of cuboids. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Surface area = total area of all faces.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A prism has the same cross-section all along; a pyramid comes to a point.
  • A net is a flat pattern that folds into a solid.
  • The surface area of a cuboid is the total area of its 6 faces: 2(lb + bh + lh).

Examples

Example

Cube with sides of 3 cm

6 faces × 9 cm²

Answer: 54 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the faces you can seeA cuboid always has 6 faces.
Confusing surface area and volumeSurface area is in cm²; volume is in cm³.
Thinking a cone is a pyramidA cone has a circular base and a curved surface.

items.q: What solid does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs (not all squares). They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: Is a cube a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 1)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 3D.

items.q: Is a cuboid a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 6)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 3D.

items.q: Is a cone a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 8)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 3D.

items.q: Is a circle a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 3)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 2D.

items.q: Is a pentagon a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 3)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 2D.

items.q: Is a rectangle a 2D shape or a 3D shape? (Shape 7)
items.e: 2D shapes are flat (length and width). 3D shapes are solid (length, width and height): 2D.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 rectangular faces, and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at one vertex, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 4 faces and all of them are triangles, so it is a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).
It has 2 flat circular faces and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is a 2-D shape.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: The two end faces are hexagons (6 sides) joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism. A hexagon is a 2-D shape.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a tetrahedron. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many edges does a tetrahedron have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: I am a 3-D shape with 6 faces. All of my faces are squares of the same size. What am I?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces that are all equal squares. A cuboid has rectangular faces.

items.q: I have 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles. What am I?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at the top make a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 4 faces, and all of them are triangles?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. A square-based pyramid has a square face as well.

items.q: What shape are the faces of a cuboid?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces (some of them can be squares, which are special rectangles).

items.q: Which of these 3-D shapes has no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over: it has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices (corners).

items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. They fold into a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: C is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: A folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which net folds into a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A has 1 square and 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. The net with only 3 triangles leaves one side open; the others make a triangular prism and a tetrahedron.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: D has 3 rectangles and 2 triangles, one triangle at each end. One wrong net has only 2 rectangles, one has both triangles at the same end, and one is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face C?
items.e: Faces C and E are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face D?
items.e: Fold the net: face C lands opposite face D. A face that touches D in the net (B, E) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face F?
items.e: Faces F and A are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: How many faces does a net of a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles: 1 + 4 = 5 faces.

items.q: Kelechi folds a net of 6 rectangles into a cuboid. How many edges does the cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 12 edges (and 6 faces and 8 vertices). 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: How many rectangles are in a net of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangle bases and 3 rectangle faces, one for each side of the triangle.

items.q: A cuboid is 3 cm by 5 cm by 8 cm. How many of its faces are 3 cm by 5 cm rectangles?
items.e: Faces come in matching pairs: 2 faces are 3 by 5, 2 are 3 by 8 and 2 are 5 by 8.

items.q: This is a net of a cuboid. Which face is the same size and shape as face A?
items.e: Face A and face D are both 3 by 4 rectangles, so they are opposite faces of the box. A box has 3 pairs of matching faces.

items.q: How many vertices does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces are the flat sides, edges are where 2 faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: What is the surface area of the cuboid made from this net?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (4 × 2) = 16. Front and back: 2 × (4 × 5) = 40. Two sides: 2 × (2 × 5) = 20. Add: 16 + 40 + 20 = 76 m².

items.q: A cube has a surface area of 96 cm². What is the area of one face?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces that are the same: 96 ÷ 6 = 16 cm². (Each edge is 4 cm, since 4 × 4 = 16.)

items.q: What is the surface area of this cuboid?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (7 × 4) = 56. Front and back: 2 × (7 × 3) = 42. Two sides: 2 × (4 × 3) = 24. Add: 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 m². Surface area covers the outside, so it is in square units, not cubic units.

items.q: This is a net of a cube. What is the surface area of the cube?
items.e: Each face is a square: 3 × 3 = 9 cm². There are 6 faces: 6 × 9 = 54 cm².

items.q: What is the surface area of the cuboid made from this net?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (4 × 3) = 24. Front and back: 2 × (4 × 8) = 64. Two sides: 2 × (3 × 8) = 48. Add: 24 + 64 + 48 = 136 cm².

items.q: This is a net of a cube. What is the surface area of the cube?
items.e: Each face is a square: 9 × 9 = 81 m². There are 6 faces: 6 × 81 = 486 m².

items.q: What is the surface area of the cuboid made from this net?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (6 × 3) = 36. Front and back: 2 × (6 × 7) = 84. Two sides: 2 × (3 × 7) = 42. Add: 36 + 84 + 42 = 162 m². Do not stop at 3 faces: each face has a matching face.

items.q: What is the surface area of the cuboid made from this net?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (12 × 6) = 144. Front and back: 2 × (12 × 8) = 192. Two sides: 2 × (6 × 8) = 96. Add: 144 + 192 + 96 = 432 cm². Do not stop at 3 faces: each face has a matching face.
